proposals.before: Sun Quan comforted him and addressed him by his courtesy name: "Chengming, Ding Fu of old was a prisoner taken at Ruo, yet King Wu of Zhou made him a field commander;
proposals.after: Sun Quan comforted him and addressed him by his courtesy name: "Chengming, Guan Dingfu of old was a prisoner taken at Ruo, yet King Wu of Chu made him a field commander;
proposals.reason: 武王 is King Wu of Chu, who appointed the Ruo captive 观丁父; the next sentences identify both men as famous Chu ministers, not Zhou figures.

proposals.before: The section assistant of Wuling, Fan You, enticed the various barbarians and plotted to attach Wuling to Liu Bei; outwardly it was reported that a difference-commander should be dispatched with ten thousand men to go punish him.
proposals.after: The section assistant of Wuling, Fan You, enticed the various barbarians and plotted to attach Wuling to Liu Bei; outwardly it was reported that a commander should be dispatched with ten thousand men to go punish him.
proposals.reason: 差督 means to dispatch a commander; 差 is not the noun “difference.”

proposals.before: Why do you make so little of him?" Sun Quan asked."
proposals.after: Sun Quan asked, "Why do you make so little of him?"
proposals.reason: The English closes the question too early and leaves a stray quotation mark after the attribution.

proposals.before: Gentleman attendant Xie Hong asked Lü Yi in passing how Chancellor Gu's case looked; Lü Yi replied that things did not look good."
proposals.after: Gentleman attendant Xie Hong asked Lü Yi in passing how Chancellor Gu's case looked; Lü Yi replied that things did not look good.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English ends with a stray closing quotation mark that is not opened and is not present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: If Gu Yong falls," Xie Hong went on, "who takes his place?" Lü Yi stayed silent until Xie Hong suggested, "I suppose Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan would be the one?" After a long pause Lü Yi admitted, "You are not far wrong."
proposals.after: "If Gu Yong falls," Xie Hong went on, "who takes his place?" Lü Yi stayed silent until Xie Hong suggested, "I suppose Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan would be the one?" After a long pause Lü Yi admitted, "You are not far wrong."
proposals.reason: The opening quotation mark before If Gu Yong falls is missing, leaving broken quotation punctuation.

proposals.before: Lu Kai, styled Jingfeng, came from Wu in Wu commandery, a kinsman of Chancellor Sun Xun.
proposals.after: Lu Kai, styled Jingfeng, came from Wu in Wu commandery, a kinsman of Chancellor Lu Xun.
proposals.reason: 丞相遜 is Lu Xun (陸遜), not a person named Sun Xun; Sun is a mistranslation of the given name Xun.

proposals.before: Lu Kai, courtesy name Jingfeng, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery, a clansman of Chancellor Sun.
proposals.after: Lu Kai, courtesy name Jingfeng, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery, a clansman of Chancellor Xun.
proposals.reason: 遜 is Xun, the given name of Lu Xun, not the surname Sun.

proposals.before: When recalled from the south he marched straight to the capital, passed through Wuchang without a backward glance, and touched none of the materiel stacked there—bold in the field, restrained before gain.
proposals.after: When summoned to go down to the capital he went straight there, passed through Wuchang without a backward glance, and took none of the weapons and military supplies—resolute in arms, restrained before gain.
proposals.reason: Chinese 被召當下，逕還赴都 means he was summoned to proceed down to the capital and went straight back there, not that he was recalled from the south.

proposals.before: Shu had veteran armies and rugged terrain; with gates barred it might have endured forever. Instead the Liu house grasped at power with fatal misjudgment, mishandled rewards and punishments, indulged in luxury, and squandered the people on needless projects—so Jin overran them and led ruler and ministers away in chains. The lesson is staring us in the face.
proposals.after: Its troops were many, picked, and strong; with gates shut and defense firm it might have been preserved for ages. Yet the Liu house, through grasping and perverse error, lost measure in rewards and punishments; the ruler gave free rein to extravagance, and the people's strength was drained on what was not urgent—so Jin attacked them and lord and ministers were taken captive. This is clear proof before our eyes.
proposals.reason: This unit continues Yizhou from the previous sentence and does not name Shu; 兵多精強 describes those armies, and 君恣意於奢侈 is the ruler's extravagance.

proposals.before: I, Pei Songzhi, gathered from travelers out of Jing and Yang Lu Kai's twenty remonstrances to Sun Hao, yet when I asked Wu natives most said they had never seen such a memorial.
proposals.after: I, Pei Songzhi, gathered from travelers out of Jing and Yang, Lu Kai's twenty remonstrances to Sun Hao, yet when I asked Wu natives most said they had never seen such a memorial.
proposals.reason: The place-name Yang is fused with Lu Kai, producing a false personal name. A comma is required after Yang.

proposals.before: When wet nurses served the princes, their husbands were excused from labor, given stipends, and sent home now and then to tend their infants.
proposals.after: When the late emperor was alive, he also nurtured the various princes and heir apparent: if wet nurses were taken, their husbands were again given corvée exemption, were granted money and goods, supplied with provisions and grain, and from time to time sent home to look on their weak young.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits 先帝在時 and the policy's attribution to the late emperor.

proposals.before: Now the overseers in each place vex the people with fussiness, and moreover there are inner agents who throw them into confusion within—one people, ten clerks—how can they bear the mandate? In the time of Emperor Jing of Han, Jiaozhi rebelled; truly it arose from this: this is following Emperor Jing's fault, not following the late emperor, seventeenth;
proposals.after: Now the overseers in each place vex the people with fussiness, and moreover there are inner agents who throw them into confusion within—one people, ten clerks—how can they bear the mandate? In the time of Emperor Jing, Jiaozhi rebelled; truly it arose from this: this is following Emperor Jing's fault, not following the late emperor, seventeenth;
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 景帝 without 漢; in this Wu memorial the Jiaozhi revolt belongs to Wu Jingdi (Sun Xiu), so of Han is an interpolation.

proposals.before: Local inspectors harrow the people, and palace agents stir trouble within—ten clerks for every household. How can the people endure? Jiaozhi rose under Emperor Jing for just such reasons. You copy Jing's error, not your father's way—that is the seventeenth count.
proposals.after: Local inspectors harrow the people, and palace agents stir trouble within—ten clerks for every household. How can the people endure? Jiaozhi rose under Emperor Jing for just such reasons. You copy Jing's error, not the late emperor's way—that is the seventeenth count.
proposals.reason: Chinese 不遵先帝 is the late emperor (Sun Quan), not Sun Hao's father.

proposals.before: Even in his father's last days, when Lü Yi and Qian Qin appeared, they were soon put to death to satisfy public outrage.
proposals.after: Even in the late emperor's closing years, when Lü Yi and Qian Qin appeared, they were soon put to death to satisfy public outrage.
proposals.reason: Chinese 先帝末年 is the late emperor's last years; Sun Hao was Sun Quan's grandson.

proposals.before: To secure the father in the capital while the heir has no foothold is the very image of sons torn from fathers and ministers torn from their lord.
proposals.after: To keep the father secure for long while leaving the son nothing to lean on is the very image of the son parted from the father and the minister parted from Your Majesty.
proposals.reason: 长安 here means long security, not a capital; the sentence answers Hao's father/son figure about the inauspicious palace.

proposals.before: To make the father secure in Chang'an while leaving the son nothing to lean on—this is the image of the son parted from the father, the minister parted from Your Majesty.
proposals.after: To make the father long secure while leaving the son nothing to lean on—this is the image of the son parted from the father, the minister parted from Your Majesty.
proposals.reason: 长安 is long peace/security, not the city Chang'an.

proposals.before: Zhu could not endure the pain of poison and confessed to what he had said.
proposals.after: Zhu could not endure the pain of the cruel torture and confessed to what he had said.
proposals.reason: 痛毒 means cruel torment in this prison narrative, not ingested poison.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yongan, he was summoned to be colonel at Xiling and enfeoffed as village marquis of the capital precinct; afterward he was transferred to colonel of the left Tiger Forest.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yongan, he was summoned to be commander of Xiling and enfeoffed as village marquis of the capital precinct; afterward he was transferred to the left Tiger Forest command.
proposals.reason: 西陵督 is a frontier commander (督), not the same office as a colonel (校尉); 左虎林 is the left Hulin post.

decisions.reason: The Chinese names 观丁父 and 武王; the following units call both men Jing worthies who became famous ministers of Chu, so this King Wu is Chu’s, not Zhou’s, and the captive’s name is Guan Dingfu, not Ding Fu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔观丁父，鄀俘也，武王以为军帅

decisions.reason: 差督督万人 is the verb 差 “to dispatch” plus a commander to lead ten thousand men; rendering 差 as the noun “difference” is a real mistranslation, and the replacement is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 外白差督督万人往讨之

decisions.reason: 权曰 opens a complete quoted question 卿何以轻之; the original English breaks the quote and leaves a stray mark after the attribution.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 权曰：「卿何以轻之？」

decisions.reason: The idiomatic line is indirect speech matching 壹答：「不能佳」, so the unopened closing quotation mark is a real English error, not a Chinese quote to preserve.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 壹答：「不能佳。」

decisions.reason: 厷又問 opens a quoted question; the English starts mid-quote without an opening mark. Adding it restores grammatical quotation without changing meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 厷又問：「若此公免退，誰當代之?」

decisions.reason: 丞相遜 is Chancellor Lu Xun (陸遜), named by office and given name; Sun Xun invents the wrong surname from 遜.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 丞相遜族子也

decisions.reason: 遜 is Lu Xun’s given name, not the surname Sun; the literal line should read Chancellor Xun, matching 丞相遜.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 丞相遜族子也

decisions.reason: 被召當下，逕還赴都 is a summons to go down to the capital and a straight journey there, not a recall from the south; 器械軍資，一無所取 and 在戎果毅 are weapons and supplies taken not at all, and resoluteness in arms.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及被召當下，逕還赴都

decisions.reason: This unit continues 益州 from the previous sentence and says 兵多精強 and 君恣意於奢侈; it does not name Shu, assign rugged terrain here, or mention chains. The replacement restores those points without adding unsupported facts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 兵多精強，閉門固守，可保萬世，而劉氏以奪乖錯，賞罰失所，君恣意於奢侈，民力竭於不急

decisions.reason: 荊、揚 are the regions Jing and Yang, after which Pei obtained 凱所諫皓二十事; without a comma, Yang Lu Kai reads as a false personal name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 予連從荊、揚來者得凱所諫皓二十事

decisions.after: When the late emperor was alive, he too provided for the princes and the heir apparent: if wet nurses were taken, their husbands were excused from labor, given money and grain, and sent home now and then to tend their infants.
decisions.reason: The original omits 先帝在時 and 亦養諸王太子, a real gap. The proposal restores those agents but is too literal for the idiomatic field and misreads 复役 as “again” rather than corvée exemption.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 先帝在時，亦養諸王太子，若取乳母，其夫復役

decisions.reason: The text has 昔景帝時，交阯反亂 with no 漢. In this Wu memorial the Jiaozhi revolt is set against 景帝 as distinct from 先帝, i.e. Wu Jingdi, so “of Han” is an interpolation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔景帝時，交阯反亂

decisions.reason: 不遵先帝 is the late emperor of the memorial’s refrain, contrasted with 遵景帝之闕. Sun Hao’s father was not that 先帝, so “your father's way” is a kinship error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是為遵景帝之闕，不遵先帝十七也

decisions.reason: 先帝末年 names the late emperor’s closing years, when 呂壹、錢欽 were killed; calling this “his father's last days” wrongly makes Sun Quan Sun Hao’s father.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 先帝末年，雖有呂壹、錢欽，尋皆誅夷

decisions.reason: 为父长安 is long security for the father, not the capital Chang’an; 使子无倚 and 臣离於陛下 are the son with nothing to lean on and the minister parted from Your Majesty.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 为父长安，使子无倚，此乃子离於父，臣离於陛下之象也

decisions.reason: 长安 here is the verb-object “long secure,” not the city Chang’an, which Wu’s court is not naming in this palace-building remonstrance.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 为父长安

decisions.reason: In this prison sequence 痛毒 is cruel torment under examination, not ingested poison; the idiomatic line already has torture, and the literal replacement matches 竺不胜痛毒.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 竺不胜痛毒，服是所道

decisions.reason: 徵為西陵督 is appointment as Xiling commander (督), not colonel (校尉); 後轉左虎林 transfers him to the left Hulin post without naming a colonelcy.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徵為西陵督，封都亭侯，後轉左虎林

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 restores the surname 观; the English personal name Ding Fu was produced by dropping 观 from 观丁父.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔观丁父

label.en: colonel of the left Tiger Forest

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0018 shows that “colonel” is not in 後轉左虎林; the office label should follow that post name without importing 校尉.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 後轉左虎林
